desc:
tasks[i] is the difficulty level of the i-th task. In one round you may complete either 2 or 3 tasks, and all tasks completed in the same round must have the same difficulty.

Return the minimum number of rounds needed to complete every task, or -1 if it is impossible.

For example, [2, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4] gives 4: the three 2s in one round, the two 3s in one round, and the five 4s in two rounds (3 + 2). The array [2, 3, 3] gives -1 because the single 2 can never be grouped.
hints: Tasks of different difficulties never share a round, so the problem splits into independent groups, one per difficulty.
For one group of size c you need the fewest numbers from {2, 3} that add up to c. When is that impossible?
Only c = 1 is impossible. Otherwise use as many 3s as possible: the answer is ceil(c / 3) rounds, because a remainder of 1 or 2 can be absorbed by turning one 3 into 2 + 2 or adding a single 2.
editorial: Count how many tasks each difficulty has. A group of size 1 cannot be completed, so the answer is -1 if any count is 1. Every size c ≥ 2 can be written as a sum of 2s and 3s: for c mod 3 = 0 use all 3s, for c mod 3 = 2 use 3s plus one 2, and for c mod 3 = 1 (with c ≥ 4) replace one 3 by two 2s, for example 7 = 3 + 2 + 2.

Since every round handles at most 3 tasks, ceil(c / 3) is also a lower bound, and the construction above reaches it in each case. Summing (c + 2) // 3 over all groups gives the answer in O(n) time with a frequency map.
